newsitem.title: USA: New Jersey's poorest city elects Hispanic mayor.
newsitem.headline: New Jersey's poorest city elects Hispanic mayor.

text.p: - A city councilman stymied Camden Mayor Arnold Webster's re-election bid Tuesday to become the first Hispanic mayor of New Jersey's poorest city.
Milton Milan, 34, won with 4,850 votes to Webster's 3,206. Three other candidates shared the remaining 4,000 votes.
Both Webster and Milan stirred up controversy.
The outgoing mayor sponsored a turkey giveaway last week, leading to accusations that he was trying to buy votes.
His successful challenger is suing the Philadelphia Inquirer newspaper for libel in connection with two articles about the 1989 murder of a drug dealer.

Despite an intense campaign, only 12,000 of Camden's 31,000 registered voters turned out for the nonpartisan election. Webster was backed by the city's Democratic organization, but Milan had the support of the vaunted Camden County machine.

Webster got some help from an unusual source when a busload of Manhattan Republicans came to Camden to work for him. "We don't recognize party lines when a candidate has good ideas for the community," David Cunningham, a Republican City Council candidate from Harlem, said.
